name: Nergal-sar-ezer
overview: Nergal-sar-ezer was a male Babylonian official who held a position of authority at the Middle Gate of Jerusalem during the Babylonian conquest, as recorded in Jeremiah 39:3. Scripture provides no information about his tribal affiliation or additional personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Nergal-sar-ezer means 'Nergal protect the prince!' This proper name reflects a Babylonian origin and invokes the god Nergal, though it was not given by God. The name is mentioned specifically in Jeremiah 39:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Nergal-sar-ezer beyond his official capacity mentioned in Jeremiah 39:3. There are no known relational connections listed.
scriptureSignificance: Nergal-sar-ezer's significance lies in his role as a Babylonian official stationed at a key entry point in Jerusalem during a pivotal moment in biblical history. His presence at the Middle Gate symbolizes the Babylonian control over Jerusalem at the time of its fall, underscoring the fulfillment of God's judgment as prophesied through Jeremiah. Though not a central character, he represents the agents of Babylonian authority during this critical period.
